name: Bloodhoof the Elder
summary: During the Lunar Festival, travelers honor Bloodhoof the Elder just north of Bloodhoof Village. The ancestral spirit appears near the bridge and offers a Coin of Ancestry in return.

sections.title: A Visit from the Ancestors
sections.body: During the Lunar Festival, spirits of heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village, near the bridge. Travelers honor the sacrifices of the past by approaching the elder, who offers words of encouragement and a Coin of Ancestry.

sections.title: The Bloodhoof Legacy
sections.body: On Mulgore's ancestral lands, Elder Bloodhoof links the living tauren tribes with the memory of their forebears. Honoring the dead is central to tauren spiritual life. It keeps the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those walking the plains in harmony.

faq.q: Where can I find Elder Bloodhoof?
faq.answer: Elder Bloodhoof appears just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, near the bridge, beneath a beam of celestial light.

faq.q: What is the purpose of seeking out Elder Bloodhoof?
faq.answer: Travelers seek Elder Bloodhoof during the Lunar Festival to honor the ancestors. In return, the spirit gives them a Coin of Ancestry and wisdom about neighboring spirits such as Elder Proudhorn.

faq.q: Why is there a beam of light shining down on him?
faq.answer: The beam of light marks Elder Bloodhoof as an ancestral spirit manifested during the Lunar Festival. It symbolizes a sacred link to the skies and the spirits of the past.

faq.q: Can Alliance characters pay homage to Elder Bloodhoof?
faq.answer: The Lunar Festival ancestors honor all mortals who show reverence, whatever their faction. Alliance travelers must tread carefully because Elder Bloodhoof is at the edge of Horde territory.

faq.q: Who is Elder Proudhorn that this elder mentions?
faq.answer: Elder Proudhorn is another ancestral spirit honored during the festival, in Thunder Bluff. Elder Bloodhoof can guide travelers to him.

faq.q: What do the Coins of Ancestry represent?
faq.answer: Coins of Ancestry are tokens of favor from Azeroth's honored spirits. They show that a traveler has honored the past, and festival celebrants trade them for festive attire, schematics, and celebratory wares.

angles.text: As a tauren, greeting Elder Bloodhoof on your home soil honors the tribe's legacy and its part in leading your people to a peaceful haven in Mulgore.
As a druid, you honor the Lunar Festival spirits and commune with the elders, strengthening your bond with the earth and stars.
As a shaman, you commune with manifest ancestors like Elder Bloodhoof, joining the living with ancestral spirits.
As an Alliance traveler, reaching Elder Bloodhoof means crossing hostile Horde plains into the heart of Mulgore.
